the development of a compression scheme that can be utilized in conjunction with XML documents to reduce the size of the documents and improve the efficiency of XML operations.

the compression scheme presented in this paper, XPack, is an efficient and flexible XML encoding system that can simultaneously support efficient storage, transmission, and processing over XML documents.
the XPack compression algorithm is a significant step towards the realization of efficient and scalable XML data management.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first compression scheme for XML documents that is both structure-aware and structure-optimized.
we are the first to propose and implement an XML compression scheme that can support efficient structure-aware queries over the compressed documents.
XPack is a high performance compression system that can be used to store and operate over Web documents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
XML documents are highly compressible when the structure of the document is taken into account.

structure-aware compression techniques can significantly improve the performance of operations over compressed documents, and that this performance improvement is especially important for applications such as mobile and pervasive computing where storage and processing power are limited.
XML document structure is a valuable resource that can be leveraged to enhance compression quality and to improve the performance of structure-aware operations over XML documents.
